Hannah —

Thanks for the brief. I ran the numbers against their workbook (attached small notes) and here is my initial recommendation (all A100-equivalent figures; we can map to H100 or Ampere flavors depending on customer preference / price):

- Sustained baseline: 12 A100-eq GPUs (sized for 120 qps @ 512 tokens, assuming ~1.6 tokens/ms throughput on our optimized kernel path)
- Burst headroom: additional 8 A100-eq GPUs for short windows (covers 350 QPS peak with <200ms p99 under continuous batching)
- Canary ramp: start at 4 A100-eq for the first 2 weeks (validate KV cache warmups, real traffic distribution), then 8 for weeks 3-4 before moving to baseline + burst config
- Disk / KV cache: need 1.2TB NVMe per node for persistent KV working set (customer provides expected dataset size in the workbook)

Operational notes / risks:
- To meet 99p <150ms at peak we may need to enforce aggressive prefix caching and shorter sequence-length defaults for Harbor. Without that SLA we should discuss a higher-cost plan or regional fallback allowances.
- If they want H100-80GB equivalents we can reduce GPU count by ~20% but cost will rise ~30% per GPU.

Estimated committed footprint to reserve today: 20 A100-eq GPUs (12 steady + 8 reserve) mapped to a dedicated SG pod; we can allow cross-region overflow to EU/US but that will increase latency for some requests.

Attaching: harbor_mop_instructions.pdf (handbook for ops-runbooks) — Marcus, once you confirm term length I can finalize node-level mapping and expected monthly unit cost.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hannah / team / Alex —

From a commercial perspective, a 12-month committed SKUs for a satellite SG pool is doable, but we need to align on three items before I can greenlight the discount:

1) Minimum commit: propose a 12-month commit at 18 A100-eq (blended) with a 10% volume discount. If engineering insists on 20 A100-eq guaranteed, discount moves to 12%.
2) SLA exception: any <150ms p99 guarantee in APAC requires a limited SLA exception clause for cross-region fallbacks. Legal needs to sign off on explicit fallback behavior.
3) Billing cadence: Harbor to accept monthly billing with a 30-day PO / net-30 payment term. Procurement, please confirm.

Attached: term_sheet_v2_redline.pdf (highlights the fallback clause we discussed).
